topic: Alabama License Requirements & Motorcycle Traffic Laws
question: Every person who operates a motor vehicle on the highways of the State of Alabama must first do what?
choice_b: Complete a written essay on road safety
explanation: Every person who operates a motor vehicle on the highways of the State of Alabama must first secure a driver license.
source_note: Alabama Motorcycle Operator Manual (18th Ed., Oct. 2024), p.2, 'License Requirements'

topic: Alabama License Requirements & Motorcycle Traffic Laws
question: How does Alabama law define a "motorcycle"?
choice_a: A motor vehicle having a seat or saddle for the rider, designed to travel on not more than three wheels in contact with the ground, excluding a tractor
choice_b: Any vehicle with fewer than four wheels regardless of engine size
choice_c: Only vehicles with an enclosed cabin
explanation: Alabama law defines a motorcycle as a motor vehicle having a seat or saddle for the use of the rider and designed to travel on not more than three wheels in contact with the ground, but excluding a tractor.
source_note: Alabama Motorcycle Operator Manual (18th Ed., Oct. 2024), p.2, 'License Requirements'

topic: Alabama License Requirements & Motorcycle Traffic Laws
question: How does Alabama law define a "motor-driven cycle"?
choice_a: Any motorcycle with an engine larger than 500cc
choice_b: Every motorcycle, including every motor scooter, with a motor producing no more than five brake horsepower or 150 cubic centimeters displacement and weighing less than 200 pounds fully equipped, and every motor-attached bicycle
explanation: A motor-driven cycle is defined as every motorcycle, including every motor scooter, with a motor which produces not more than five brake horsepower nor more than 150 cubic centimeter engine displacement and weighs less than 200 pounds fully equipped, and every bicycle with a motor attached.
source_note: Alabama Motorcycle Operator Manual (18th Ed., Oct. 2024), p.2, 'License Requirements'

topic: Alabama License Requirements & Motorcycle Traffic Laws
question: At what age, and with what license, may a person operate either a motorcycle or motor-driven cycle in Alabama?
choice_c: Age 16, with a Class M driver license
explanation: A person who has attained the age of 16 and has been issued a Class M driver license may operate either a motorcycle or motor-driven cycle.
source_note: Alabama Motorcycle Operator Manual (18th Ed., Oct. 2024), p.2, 'License Requirements'

topic: Alabama License Requirements & Motorcycle Traffic Laws
question: What may a person who is at least 14 years of age apply for in Alabama?
choice_a: A full Class M license with no restrictions
choice_c: A license to operate any motorcycle regardless of engine size
choice_d: A restricted license to operate a motor-driven cycle only
explanation: A person who is at least 14 years of age may apply for a restricted license to operate a motor-driven cycle only.
source_note: Alabama Motorcycle Operator Manual (18th Ed., Oct. 2024), p.2, 'License Requirements'

topic: Alabama License Requirements & Motorcycle Traffic Laws
question: Under Alabama law, how is a moped classified?
choice_b: As a bicycle with no licensing requirements at all
choice_c: As a full motorcycle requiring a Class M endorsement with no restrictions
explanation: Under Alabama law, a moped is considered a motor-driven cycle.
source_note: Alabama Motorcycle Operator Manual (18th Ed., Oct. 2024), p.2, 'License Requirements'

topic: Alabama License Requirements & Motorcycle Traffic Laws
question: Once a 14-year-old is licensed to operate a motor-driven cycle, how long is that restricted license valid for that class of vehicle?
explanation: Once a 14-year-old is licensed to operate a motor-driven cycle, the license is valid for a four-year period for that class vehicle.
source_note: Alabama Motorcycle Operator Manual (18th Ed., Oct. 2024), p.2, 'License Requirements'

topic: Alabama License Requirements & Motorcycle Traffic Laws
question: What restriction applies to a 14- or 15-year-old's motor-driven cycle license in Alabama?
choice_a: No restrictions apply at any age
choice_b: They may only ride with a licensed adult passenger
choice_c: Restriction "B" -- limited to a motor-driven cycle of 5 horsepower or smaller
choice_d: They may only ride between 6 a.m. and 6 p.m.
explanation: Restriction "B" (motor-driven cycle - 5 horsepower or smaller - for ages 14 and 15 only) applies once a 14-year-old is licensed, until the applicant returns at age 16 to transfer to an unrestricted motorcycle class license.
source_note: Alabama Motorcycle Operator Manual (18th Ed., Oct. 2024), p.2, 'License Requirements'

topic: Alabama License Requirements & Motorcycle Traffic Laws
question: What does Alabama law require regarding carrying and displaying your driver license?
choice_a: The license only needs to be kept at home
choice_b: A photograph of the license on a phone is never acceptable under any circumstance
choice_c: Only out-of-state riders must carry their license
choice_d: Every driver must have their license in possession at all times when operating a motor vehicle and display it upon demand of a judge, peace officer, or state trooper
explanation: Alabama law requires every driver to have their driver license in possession at all times when operating a motor vehicle and to display it upon the demand of a judge of any court, a peace officer, or a state trooper.
source_note: Alabama Motorcycle Operator Manual (18th Ed., Oct. 2024), p.2, 'License to Be Carried and Exhibited on Demand'

topic: Alabama License Requirements & Motorcycle Traffic Laws
question: Under Alabama law, are motorcycles entitled to full use of a traffic lane?
choice_a: Yes -- no motor vehicle shall be driven so as to deprive a motorcycle of the full use of a lane
choice_b: No, motorcycles must share a lane with other vehicles at all times
explanation: All motorcycles are entitled to full use of traffic lanes, and no motor vehicle shall be driven in such a manner as to deprive any motorcycle of the full use of a lane (this does not apply to motorcycles operated two abreast in a single lane).
source_note: Alabama Motorcycle Operator Manual (18th Ed., Oct. 2024), p.3, 'Motorcycle Operation in Alabama'

topic: Alabama License Requirements & Motorcycle Traffic Laws
question: May the operator of a motorcycle overtake and pass another vehicle within the same lane occupied by that vehicle?
choice_b: No -- the operator shall not overtake and pass in the same lane occupied by the vehicle being overtaken
choice_d: Yes, if the horn is sounded first
explanation: The operator of a motorcycle shall not overtake and pass in the same lane occupied by the vehicle being overtaken.
source_note: Alabama Motorcycle Operator Manual (18th Ed., Oct. 2024), p.3, 'Motorcycle Operation in Alabama'

topic: Alabama License Requirements & Motorcycle Traffic Laws
question: Under Alabama law, is it legal to operate a motorcycle between lanes of traffic or between rows of vehicles (lane splitting)?
choice_b: Yes, on any road with a posted speed limit over 55 mph
choice_c: No -- no person shall operate a motorcycle between lanes of traffic or between rows of vehicles
choice_d: Yes, but only in construction zones
explanation: No person shall operate a motorcycle between lanes of traffic or between rows of vehicles -- lane splitting is prohibited under Alabama law.
source_note: Alabama Motorcycle Operator Manual (18th Ed., Oct. 2024), p.3, 'Motorcycle Operation in Alabama'

topic: Alabama License Requirements & Motorcycle Traffic Laws
question: What is the maximum number of motorcycles that may be operated abreast in a single lane under Alabama law?
choice_b: One -- riding abreast is never permitted
explanation: Motorcycles shall not be operated more than two abreast in a single lane.
source_note: Alabama Motorcycle Operator Manual (18th Ed., Oct. 2024), p.3, 'Motorcycle Operation in Alabama'

topic: Alabama License Requirements & Motorcycle Traffic Laws
question: Under Alabama law, may a person riding upon a motorcycle attach themselves or the motorcycle to another vehicle on the roadway?
choice_a: No -- no person riding upon a motorcycle shall attach themselves or the motorcycle to any other vehicle on a roadway
choice_b: Yes, as long as a rope or strap is used
explanation: No person riding upon a motorcycle shall attach themselves or the motorcycle to any other vehicle on a roadway.
source_note: Alabama Motorcycle Operator Manual (18th Ed., Oct. 2024), p.3, 'Motorcycle Operation in Alabama'

topic: Alabama License Requirements & Motorcycle Traffic Laws
question: Under Alabama law, on what permanent and regular part of a motorcycle must a cyclist ride?
choice_a: Anywhere the rider finds comfortable, including the fuel tank
choice_b: Only upon the permanent and regular seat, and not carry another person unless the cycle has footpegs for more than one person
choice_c: Standing on the footrests at all times
explanation: Cyclists shall ride only upon the permanent and regular seat and shall not carry any other person unless the cycle is designed and equipped with footpegs to carry more than one person.
source_note: Alabama Motorcycle Operator Manual (18th Ed., Oct. 2024), p.3, 'Motorcycle Operation in Alabama'

topic: Alabama License Requirements & Motorcycle Traffic Laws
question: Which basic rules of the road apply to motorcycles, motor-driven cycles, and mopeds in Alabama?
choice_a: None -- cyclists follow a completely separate traffic code
choice_c: All the basic rules of the road in the Alabama traffic code apply to them, as well as to other vehicles
choice_d: Only rules for commercial vehicles apply
explanation: All the basic rules of the road in the Alabama traffic code apply to motorcycles, motor-driven cycles, and mopeds, as well as other vehicles, with additional laws that apply specifically to cyclists.
source_note: Alabama Motorcycle Operator Manual (18th Ed., Oct. 2024), p.3, 'Motorcycle Operation in Alabama'
